source: ដំណាំទុរេន (Durian Cultivation), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, 2015, 31pp
text: In the establishment period, the source emphasizes mulching around the young tree's base with organic material (straw, dried grass, rice husk) to conserve soil moisture and suppress weeds, while keeping a small clear gap immediately around the trunk itself so the mulch does not hold constant moisture against the bark, echoing the same collar-rot caution given in Source A. Weeding should be done regularly, ideally by hand or shallow hoeing near the trunk to avoid root damage, since durian's feeder roots are relatively shallow and easily injured by deep cultivation close to the trunk.
